name: Narayana Hrudayalaya Limited
moat: India's largest cardiac care network by volume: 42 facilities and ~5,550 operational beds in India (18 hospitals, 2 heart centres, 20 clinics) plus 2 Cayman hospitals, and since Nov-2025 the UK Practice Plus Group (12 facilities, 330 beds, ~93% NHS-contracted). Founded by Dr. Devi Shetty — brand trust in cardiac and oncology is irreplaceable; Health City Cayman is a unique medical-tourism moat.
leadership: Largest cardiac surgery network in India (2,137 cardiac surgeries at NICS Bengaluru in Q1 FY27 alone). FY26 revenue ₹7,896 Cr (+44% YoY), PAT ₹806 Cr, OPM 21%. Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹2,684 Cr (+78% YoY; India +17%, Cayman +39%, UK ₹826 Cr), EBITDA ₹505 Cr (18.8% margin), PAT ₹207 Cr (+5.7%).
non_rep: Volume-driven cost leadership in cardiac surgery — performs procedures at a fraction of US cost. Cayman hospital serves US/UK patients at 40-60% savings; UK PPGHL adds long-term NHS contracts (£250m revenue). Cannot be replicated without decades of surgical volume and payer relationships.
tailwinds: India private healthcare demand surge
Medical tourism from UK/USA via Cayman
NHS waiting-list outsourcing feeding UK PPGHL volumes
Rising cardiac disease incidence in India
Health insurance penetration growth
risks: UK PPGHL is low-margin (FY25 adj. EBITDA £20m on £250m revenue) and dilutes group margin
Gross borrowings ₹5,858 Cr (Mar-26) with US$115m + £150m FX debt; debt guided to rise for 2-3 years
Competition from Max Healthcare and Apollo
Margin pressure from staff costs and integrated-care/insurance losses
track: India hospital EBITDA margin (+400 bps YoY in Q1 FY27) and ARPOB growth
UK PPGHL EBITDA improvement and payer-mix shift to private/self-pay
Net debt trajectory vs ₹3,000 Cr committed capex (Southwest Bangalore 100 beds by end Q2 FY27)
Cayman insurance (One Health) losses narrowing toward breakeven
change_remark: Moved red_flags.financial 8 to 7 and comp.capital 7.0 to 6.5 (q 8.1 to 8.0): Mar-26 borrowings ₹5,858 Cr vs ₹2,428 Cr after the ₹2,200 Cr Practice Plus Group UK acquisition (Nov-2025), FX debt US$115m + £150m, FY26 ROCE 16% vs 21%, and management guiding on the 3 Aug 2026 call that debt rises for 2-3 more years; net D/E 0.42 at 30 Jun 2026 keeps this moderate. Q1 FY27 (31 Jul 2026) revenue ₹2,684 Cr +78%, PAT +5.7%, India EBITDA margin +400 bps; ICRA AA Stable reaffirmed 19 Jan 2026; promoter 63.27% unpledged. Conviction 8 and HOLD unchanged.

name: HealthCare Global Enterprises Limited
moat: India's largest dedicated cancer care network — the most AERB-licensed private cancer centres in the country, with linear accelerators, PET-CT, tomotherapy/MR-Linac, surgical robots and bone-marrow transplant units; Milann fertility brand alongside. Oncology requires highly specialised equipment plus multidisciplinary teams that take years to build.
leadership: #1 dedicated oncology hospital chain in India. FY26 revenue ₹2,538 Cr (+14% YoY), OPM 18%, PAT ₹23 Cr. Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹695 Cr (+13% YoY, patient volumes +11%), adjusted EBITDA ₹134 Cr (+20%, 19.4% margin), PAT ₹14 Cr vs ₹5 Cr. KKR-controlled since 2025 (took over from CVC/Aceso); new North Bangalore hospital commissioned Q1 FY27.
non_rep: Oncology is the highest-barrier medical specialty — AERB radiation licences, regulatory approvals, specialist oncologist concentration (20 added in the last 4-5 months to Aug-26) and equipment capex of ₹50-100 Cr per centre. Cannot be replicated quickly.
tailwinds: Cancer incidence in India growing 12% p.a.
Tier-2/3 city cancer care deficit
Health insurance covering oncology; non-institutional payer mix up to 69% (Q1 FY27)
Early detection technology adoption
risks: High capex per new centre; North Bangalore ramp-up losses peaked in Q1 FY27
Specialist oncologist supply constraint
Competition from Apollo Proton Centre and multi-specialty majors
Government scheme price caps (CGHS) and low-margin chemo drug exits trimming revenue
Thin PAT (FY26 ₹23 Cr) with D/E ~1.3x and low interest cover
track: North Bangalore hospital loss reduction and EBITDA breakeven timeline
Adjusted EBITDA margin path toward 21-22% guidance (2 years) from 19.4% in Q1 FY27
ARPP growth (only +2% in Q1 FY27) and occupancy at existing centres
CDSCO ethics-committee CAPA compliance and any further regulatory action
change_remark: No material change — all pillars, categories and comps retained. Checked: Q1 FY27 results/concall 7 Aug 2026 (revenue ₹695 Cr +13%, volumes +11%, adj. EBITDA ₹134 Cr +20% at 19.4%, PAT ₹14 Cr vs ₹5 Cr; guidance 21-22% EBITDA margin in 2 years, 24-25% in 4-5 years); FY26 PAT ₹23 Cr vs ₹49 Cr, ROE 2.5%, borrowings ₹1,735 Cr; CDSCO 24-month ethics-committee suspension (12 Jun 2026) already in governance 4; promoter 64.21% (Jun-26) after the ₹425 Cr rights issue approved 18 Feb 2026. One improved quarter is not yet sustained, so execution stays 5; HOLD unchanged.

name: Syrma SGS Technology Limited
moat: Design-led Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS/ODM) player: ODM ~17% of revenue and exports ~24% (Q1 FY27), RFID via Perfect ID, medical devices via Johari MedTech, defence platform acquired, Kaga (Japan) JV signed FY27 and a bare-PCB plant under ECMS due for commercial production Apr-2027. Ranjangaon campus is India's first full EMS campus.
leadership: Mid-size Indian EMS/ODM leader. FY26 revenue ₹4,819 Cr (+27% YoY), OPM 11% (9% FY25), PAT ₹346 Cr (+88%). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹1,589 Cr (+68% YoY), OPM 10%, PAT ₹106 Cr (+112%); order book ~₹6,770 Cr (10-10.5 months execution). Serves auto, consumer (~30%), industrial, healthcare (~7-8%), IT/railways and exports.
non_rep: Design-led ODM capability (target 25% of sales) differentiates from pure assembly players; RFID (Perfect ID) is a niche with few Indian competitors; MedTech EMS (Jodhpur expansion) and the backward-integrated PCB plant under ECMS give an early-mover cost/quality edge that takes years and ₹1,000 Cr+ of capital to copy.
tailwinds: India PLI/ECMS incentives for electronics and PCB manufacturing
China+1 sourcing by global OEMs; exports +61% YoY in Q1 FY27
RFID adoption in retail/logistics/healthcare
Medical electronics domestic manufacturing (MedTech ~50% growth guided)
risks: EMS is low-margin by nature — execution dependent (FY27 EBITDA margin guided 10.5-11%)
Customer concentration risk
Working capital creeping up: NWC days 63 to 71 in Q1 FY27 on 'strategic inventory'
West Asia supply-chain/component lead-time risk flagged by management (Aug-26)
Repeated equity dilution: ₹1,000 Cr QIP Aug-2025, fresh ₹1,000 Cr enabling QIP approved 25 Aug 2026
track: Revenue per segment (auto/consumer/medical/RFID/export mix) and ODM share vs 17-19% near-term target
OPM vs 10.5-11% FY27 guidance and gross margin trajectory
PCB plant milestones: equipment Oct-26, power-on Jan-Mar 27, commercial production Apr-27
Working-capital days and inventory normalisation by end-CY26
change_remark: Moved execution 7 to 8 (Q1 FY27 results 3 Aug 2026: revenue ₹1,589 Cr +68%, PAT ₹106 Cr +112%, 35%+ FY27 guidance to be exceeded; order book ₹6,770 Cr), capital_allocation 6 to 6.5 and red_flags.financial 6 to 7 (Ind-Ra upgrade to IND AA/Stable 5 May 2026; borrowings ₹400 Cr vs ₹665 Cr, FY26 FCF +₹114 Cr), ownership_behaviour 5 to 5.5 (Sep-25 drop was QIP dilution; flat at 42.28% since, no pledge), comp.capital 5.0 to 5.5, q 6.6 to 6.8. Unlisted VVDN swapped for PG Electroplast. Conviction 7, HOLD unchanged; watch NWC days 71 and ₹1,000 Cr enabling QIP (Aug-2026).

name: MTAR Technologies Limited
moat: Ultra-precision critical components for nuclear, defence, space and clean energy — one of the top-3 precision suppliers to India's civil nuclear (NPCIL), space (ISRO) and defence (DRDO) programmes, and a long-standing fuel-cell hot-box supplier to Bloom Energy (USA). Nuclear components require AERB certification — a near-impenetrable regulatory moat; new Products division (ball/roller screws, actuators) and export-only data-centre infrastructure add adjacencies.
leadership: Only listed Indian company making fuel-cell components for Bloom Energy; nuclear components supplier to NPCIL (record Kaiga 5&6 inflows; ₹126.74 Cr coolant-channel order 26 Aug 2026). FY26 revenue ₹876 Cr (+30% YoY), OPM 20%, PAT ₹95 Cr (+76%). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹361 Cr (+130% YoY), EBITDA ₹85 Cr (23.5%), PAT ₹50 Cr (+365%); order book ₹5,143 Cr plus ~₹800 Cr announced 18 Aug 2026 — roughly 6x FY26 revenue.
non_rep: Tolerances of 1-5 microns on nuclear and space components — requires 20+ years of metrology expertise across seven Hyderabad units plus a dedicated export facility. AERB nuclear certification and ISRO/NPCIL vendor qualification take 5-8 years; Bloom Energy qualification built over a decade.
tailwinds: India nuclear energy expansion (Kaiga 5&6 orders; fleet-mode 700 MW PHWRs)
Green hydrogen / fuel cell and AI data-centre power demand for Bloom Energy
India space privatisation (NSIL, IN-SPACe)
Defence indigenisation — A&D revenue guided to double in FY27
risks: Bloom Energy concentration risk (clean energy still the largest vertical; ~70% of planned capex)
Nuclear project delays (long gestation; orders executable to 2028)
Promoter stake keeps falling (29.35% at Jun-26) with a small promoter pledge rolled 28 Aug 2026
Working-capital intensity historically extreme (FY26 inventory 397 days, debtor days 140)
Geopolitical risk on defence exports
track: Execution against FY27 guidance of ~80% revenue growth and 24% EBITDA margin (management expects to beat)
Order book conversion and Bloom Energy share of revenue
Working-capital days holding near 59 (Q1 FY27) vs 100-day year-end target
₹500 Cr two-year capex (70:30 clean energy vs others) and promoter selling/pledge trend
change_remark: Moved execution 6 to 7.5 (Q1 FY27 call 18 Aug 2026: revenue ₹361 Cr +130%, PAT ₹50 Cr +365%, EBITDA margin 23.5%, order book ₹5,143 Cr + ₹800 Cr, WC days 59 vs 172), capital_allocation 5 to 5.5 and red_flags.financial 6 to 6.5 (ICRA upgrade to A+ Stable 7 Jul 2026; FY26 CFO ₹192 Cr vs PAT ₹95 Cr). Cut ownership_behaviour 4 to 3.5 and red_flags.governance 6 to 5.5: promoter holding 30.44% to 29.35% (Jun-26) after May-Jun 2026 sales and a 1,05,000-share pledge rolled 28 Aug 2026. comp.capital 5.0 to 5.5, q 7.9 to 8.0; conviction 8, HOLD unchanged.

name: DEE DEVELOPMENT ENG LTD
moat: India's largest process-piping fabricator by installed capacity (93,500 MTPA piping + 32,400 MTPA heavy fabrication across 7 facilities in India and Thailand) for oil & gas, refining, petrochemicals, fertilisers, power and nuclear. IBR-certified and ASME-approved — a regulatory moat in a safety-critical segment, now backward-integrated with an Anjar seamless-pipe plant (commissioned Mar-2026).
leadership: Niche leader in high-pressure process piping. FY26 revenue ₹1,142 Cr (+38% YoY), OPM 17%, PAT ₹77 Cr (+75%). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹294 Cr (+32%), operating EBITDA ₹50 Cr (16.9%), PAT ₹16 Cr; order book ₹2,428 Cr at Jun-26 incl. a ₹387 Cr BPCL piping contract; FY27 guidance ₹1,500 Cr+ revenue at >19% EBITDA margin. Serves IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, ONGC, NTPC and global EPCs.
non_rep: IBR/ASME certifications for high-pressure piping require years of audit trails and project history; customer qualification cycles for refinery/nuclear piping take 2-3 years. Port-adjacent Anjar platform (Kandla/Mundra) plus captive P-92 seamless pipe capacity are hard for smaller fabricators to match.
tailwinds: India refinery and petrochemical capex cycle (BPCL ₹387 Cr order, FY27 inflows guided >₹2,000 Cr)
Thermal power revival — P-92 high-wall-thickness boiler piping demand
Fertilizer plant modernization
LNG terminal and nuclear piping
risks: Project-based lumpy revenue (₹25 Cr dispatches deferred in Q1 FY27 on Middle East disruptions)
Raw material (alloy steel) cost pressure and FX volatility
Weak cash conversion: FY26 CFO ₹20 Cr vs PAT ₹77 Cr, FCF -₹165 Cr
Top-10 customers ~58% of revenue (FY25); competition from Welspun/ISGEC on large fabrication
Non-core biomass power: tariff litigation and Malwa Power impairment uncertainty flagged by auditors
track: Order book (₹2,428 Cr) conversion and FY27 revenue vs ₹1,500 Cr+ guidance
EBITDA margin vs >19% guidance (Q1 FY27 only 16.9%) as Anjar utilisation rises to 60-65%
Debt reduction after ₹225 Cr prepayment from the Jul-2026 preferential issue; CFO/PAT recovery
Seamless pipe plant ramp (target ~20% EBITDA, 50:50 captive vs external)
change_remark: Moved execution 6 to 6.5 (FY26 revenue +38%/PAT +75%; Q1 FY27 results 4-5 Aug 2026 revenue ₹294 Cr +32%, EBITDA +39%; order book ₹2,428 Cr at Jun-26 with ₹387 Cr BPCL win; FY27 guidance ₹1,500 Cr+ at >19% margin), capital_allocation 4 to 4.5 and red_flags.financial 5 to 5.5 (₹300 Cr preferential allotment completed 9 Jul 2026, ~₹225 Cr for debt prepayment; first dividend, 9% payout), comp.capital 4.0 to 4.5, comp.growth 4.9 to 5.5, q 5.8 to 6.0. Promoter 70.18% to 65.13% (Jul-26) is pure dilution — ownership 6 kept. FY26 FCF -₹165 Cr keeps conviction 6 and HOLD.

name: Hitachi Energy India Limited
moat: India subsidiary of Hitachi Energy (Japan/Switzerland) — transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems, grid automation, power quality and now BESS (first 165 MW/330 MWh order, Q1 FY27). HVDC technology is near-exclusive globally — only Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy and GE Vernova can deliver it — and India's renewable grid needs HVDC corridors.
leadership: Leader in high-voltage transmission equipment in India. FY26 revenue ₹8,148 Cr (+28% YoY), OPM 16% (9% FY25), PAT ₹988 Cr (+157%). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹2,494 Cr (+69% YoY), operational EBITDA ₹400 Cr (16.0%), PAT ₹294 Cr (+123%); orders ₹5,097 Cr (+26% ex-HVDC) and record backlog ₹32,222 Cr (~3.5x TTM revenue). 71.31% held by Hitachi Energy; 20th factory (Karjan LPT) under construction since Jun-2026.
non_rep: HVDC has only 3-4 global suppliers; India's 500 GW-by-2030 and 900 GW non-fossil-by-FY36 targets require HVDC corridors where Hitachi Energy is the incumbent supplier. Decades of grid engineering relationships with PGCIL plus 20 Indian factories and parent technology transfer cannot be replicated by domestic entrants.
tailwinds: India 500 GW renewable target by 2030 (900 GW non-fossil by FY36)
HVDC inter-state transmission corridors
AI data centre power infrastructure — largest order contributor in Q1 FY27
Exports (33.6% of Q1 FY27 orders ex-HVDC) and BESS/smart-grid adoption
risks: Premium valuation (P/E ~120)
Parent Hitachi Energy related-party reliance and global restructuring risk
Execution on large HVDC projects and ₹4,000 Cr capex programme
Geopolitical tension/tariffs slowing the global energy-transition pace (management outlook Aug-2026)
track: Order inflows from PGCIL/state utilities and data centres; backlog ₹32,222 Cr conversion
HVDC and BESS project awards
Revenue growth sustaining >30% YoY with operational EBITDA margin >=16%
Karjan LPT factory commissioning timeline
change_remark: No material change — all pillars, categories, comps (q 8.9), conviction 9 and HOLD retained. Facts checked: Q1 FY27 press release 7 Aug 2026 (revenue ₹2,494 Cr +69% YoY, operational EBITDA ₹400 Cr at 16.0%, PAT ₹294 Cr +123%, orders ₹5,097 Cr +26% ex-HVDC, record backlog ₹32,222 Cr, first 165 MW/330 MWh BESS order); FY26 revenue ₹8,148 Cr, PAT ₹988 Cr, ROCE 29.4%, borrowings ₹86 Cr; Karjan LPT plant started Jun-2026 within a ₹4,000 Cr capex plan; promoter steady at 71.31% (Jun-26), no pledge; AGM and RPT postal ballot 28 Aug 2026; CRISIL ESG 69 (2 Sep 2026).

name: Astra Microwave Products Limited
moat: India's premier RF/microwave subsystem manufacturer for defence — missiles, radar (incl. HAL's Uttam AESA radar), electronic warfare and satellite systems — with 30+ years of DRDO/HAL/BEL/ISRO relationships (35 radars, 25 satellites, ~15 strategic programmes). Only listed pure-play Indian defence-electronics company at this depth; space & meteorology unit to be demerged into a separate listed entity.
leadership: Supplies DRDO, HAL, BEL, BDL, ISRO/SAC and exports. FY26 revenue ₹1,163 Cr (+11% YoY), OPM 29%, PAT ₹193 Cr (+25%). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹177 Cr (-11% YoY on approval/inspection delays), OPM 19%, PAT ₹12 Cr; record order book ~₹4,300 Cr after the ~₹2,205 Cr HAL Uttam radar order (Jul-2026); FY27 guidance raised to ~₹1,350 Cr (+15-20%), FY28 ~₹1,600 Cr.
non_rep: RF/microwave components for missiles and AESA radars require rigorous qualification — MIL-STD testing, DRDO empanelment and years of co-development history (Uttam radar subsystems built over a decade). Technology cannot be imported easily due to dual-use export controls.
tailwinds: India defence capex ₹6.2 Lakh Cr over 5 years; HAL Uttam radar programme (12 units by Sep-2027, 25+/yr after)
Atmanirbhar Bharat indigenisation mandate — Tejas, Su-30, LCH, AMCA pipelines
Missile programme acceleration (QRSAM, Astra, MRSAM)
Electronic warfare, counter-drone and space (own satellite planned within 6 months)
risks: Government payment delays on defence contracts (debtor days 216 in FY26)
Project-based lumpy revenues — Q1 FY27 revenue -11% on inspection/approval delays
Concentration: ~66% of standalone backlog is defence; Uttam order dominates the book
Execution/leadership transition — MD S. Gurunatha Reddy exits 30 Sep 2026; demerger execution risk
Competition from BEL in select subsystems
track: Order book (₹4,300 Cr) execution and FY27 order inflow target of ~₹1,600 Cr ex-Uttam
FY27 revenue vs ₹1,350 Cr guidance; H2 catch-up of Q1 slippage
Receivables/working capital as Uttam execution ramps (management expects pressure later in FY27)
Space & meteorology demerger milestones and MD transition from 1 Oct 2026
change_remark: Moved execution 7 to 7.5 (record ~₹2,205 Cr HAL Uttam radar order Jul-2026 lifting the order book to ~₹4,300 Cr; FY27 guidance raised to ~₹1,350 Cr, +15-20%, on the 11 Aug 2026 call), capital_allocation 7 to 7.5 and red_flags.financial 6 to 6.5 (FY26 CFO ₹387 Cr vs PAT ₹193 Cr, borrowings cut to ₹288 Cr, CRISIL upgrade to A+/Stable 31 Aug 2026), comp.capital 7.0 to 7.5, q 8.2 to 8.3. Promoter stake corrected to 6.54% (flat since Mar-24). Watch Q1 FY27 revenue -11%, MD transition (1 Oct 2026) and space-unit demerger; conviction 8, HOLD unchanged.

name: Aster DM Healthcare Limited
moat: Now Aster DM Quality Care (merger with Blackstone-backed Quality Care India effective 1 Jul 2026; renamed 3 Jul 2026) — one of India's three largest hospital platforms (~38 hospitals, ~10,900 beds across Kerala, Karnataka, AP/Telangana, MP and other Tier-2/3 markets) plus clinics, pharmacies and labs. Strong Kerala/South India brand; pure-India focus since the 2024 GCC divestiture is delivering 22% EBITDA margins.
leadership: Top-3 Indian hospital chain by beds. Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) combined proforma revenue ₹2,597 Cr (+20% YoY), EBITDA ₹576 Cr (+30%, 22.2% margin), patient volumes 2 Mn (+13%), blended occupancy 64% (+510 bps); Aster platform revenue ₹1,311 Cr (+22%), normalised PAT ₹125 Cr (+39%; reported ₹29 Cr after ₹114 Cr merger costs). FY26 (Aster India) revenue ₹4,643 Cr (+12%), OPM 19%, PAT ₹427 Cr. 4,170+ beds to be added over 3-4 years to exceed 15,000.
non_rep: Kerala is deeply penetrated — brand loyalty and doctor networks are sticky; QCIL adds CARE/KIMS Health franchises in Hyderabad, Vizag and Tier-2 towns. Pharmacy/clinic network feeds hospital referrals; a 45,000-strong clinical workforce and 10,900-bed scale with 53% brownfield expansion pipeline cannot be assembled quickly.
tailwinds: India healthcare spending growth and insurance penetration
Merger synergies — 10-15% incremental EBITDA targeted from FY27
Medical value travel (MVT revenue +62% YoY in Q1 FY27)
Brownfield bed additions: Trivandrum (Jan-2027), Hyderabad (Apr-2027), Sarjapur (H2 FY28)
risks: Post-merger integration of two platforms and 45,000 staff; synergies yet to show
Blackstone co-promoter (~30%) is a financial investor with an eventual exit overhang
Doctor attrition risk (Karnataka attrition hit FY26 before recovering)
Non-core capital outlays — USD 44.1m (~₹479 Cr) for 14.21% of Bangladesh's STS Holdings (28 Aug 2026)
Competition in Bengaluru/Hyderabad from Apollo, Manipal, Narayana
track: Combined EBITDA margin path from 22.2% toward 24-25% target in 3 years
Synergy delivery (10-15% incremental EBITDA) and occupancy (64% blended)
New hospital commissioning: Trivandrum H2 FY27, Hyderabad Apr-2027; capex vs net debt ₹1,162 Cr
Blackstone/Moopen shareholding moves and related-party transactions
change_remark: Major event: Aster-Quality Care merger effective 1 Jul 2026 (renamed 3 Jul 2026; promoter group 40.39% to 53.72% with Blackstone). Moved conviction 6 to 7, execution 7 to 8 (Q1 FY27 call 5 Aug 2026: proforma revenue ₹2,597 Cr +20%, EBITDA ₹576 Cr +30%, margin 22.2%), red_flags.financial 7 to 7.5 (CRISIL AA+/Stable assigned 30 Jul 2026; net debt ₹1,162 Cr), comps moat 6.5 to 7.0, mgmt 6.0 to 6.5, capital 5.0 to 5.5, q 6.3 to 6.8, durability Stable to Widening. Governance held pending clarity on the USD 44.1m STS Holdings (Bangladesh) stake bought 28 Aug 2026. HOLD unchanged.

name: NEPHROCARE HEALTH SERV L
moat: Asia's largest dialysis chain — 550 clinics across 357 cities in 5 countries (487 India, 51 Philippines, plus Uzbekistan, Nepal, 1 in KSA) serving 38,262 active patients and 10.3 lakh treatments in Q1 FY27 alone. Asset-light formats (272 captive hospital clinics, 200 PPP units, 78 standalone), proprietary Renova dialyzer reprocessing, RenAssure protocols and the NephroPlus Index create a clinical-standardisation moat. IPO Dec 2025 at ₹460/share.
leadership: #5 globally by treatments; only Indian dialysis company scaled internationally (international 45% of revenue vs 30% eighteen months earlier). FY26 revenue ₹999 Cr (+32% YoY), EBITDA ₹227 Cr (23%), PAT ₹77 Cr. Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹282 Cr (+24%), adj. EBITDA ₹65 Cr (23.1%, +120 bps), PAT ₹32 Cr (+35%), adj. PAT ₹37 Cr (+42%); revenue per treatment ₹2,733 (+9%). Backed by Bessemer, Quadria, IFC; entering Kazakhstan (Almaty acquisition, 1 Sep 2026).
non_rep: Dialysis patients are chronic — once enrolled, switching is rare (medical continuity). Network density creates route and procurement efficiency; India's US$22/treatment price point forces a cost discipline that earns superior margins when exported to better-reimbursed markets. PPP contracts with government hospitals are long-term and sticky; in-house NIDA nursing academy (first batch Q3 FY27) eases the trained-nurse constraint.
tailwinds: India CKD incidence growing — 17% of adults affected; diabetes/hypertension pipeline
Government Ayushman Bharat and PPP dialysis coverage
Higher-realisation international markets (Philippines ~900 fragmented clinics; Saudi MoH tenders; Kazakhstan entry)
Dialysis market consolidation away from standalone centres
risks: Reimbursement rate and payment-cycle risk from government schemes (receivables ₹317 Cr, ~116 debtor days)
International expansion execution — Saudi JV losses (₹3.6 Cr share of loss in Q1 FY27), Uzbekistan tax assessment ₹14.79 Cr (31 Aug 2026)
High patient acquisition cost and nurse availability
PE-investor exit overhang post Dec-2025 IPO
track: Patient (guest) and treatment additions per quarter; 40-50 India and 10-15 Philippines clinic adds per year
Adjusted EBITDA margin (23.1% in Q1 FY27) as international mix rises
Saudi Arabia tender outcome and JV losses; Uzbekistan tax appeal
Government PPP receivable days and cash conversion
change_remark: Moved execution 6 to 7 (Q1 FY27 call 12 Aug 2026: revenue ₹282 Cr +24%, adj. EBITDA ₹65 Cr at 23.1%, adj. PAT +42%, 26 clinics added; FY26 revenue +32%), capital_allocation 6 to 6.5 and red_flags.financial 6 to 7 (borrowings ₹80 Cr vs ₹261 Cr, FY26 CFO ₹233 Cr, FCF ₹113 Cr), comp.capital 6.0 to 6.5, comp.growth 5.5 to 6.5, q 6.2 to 6.6; confidence raised Low to Moderate after three post-listing concalls. Governance kept at 6, noting the ₹14.79 Cr Uzbekistan tax assessment (31 Aug 2026) and ₹230 ESOP grant (3 Sep 2026). Conviction 6, HOLD unchanged.

name: Neuland Laboratories Limited
moat: Pure-play API CDMO with 360+ scientists across three segments: CMS (custom manufacturing for innovators, now the majority of revenue), GDS (prime and specialty generic APIs) and peptides — commercial-scale peptide facility due for commissioning Sep-2026. US FDA, EDQM and PMDA approved; Unit 3 cleared an FDA inspection (10-14 Aug 2026) with a single Form 483 observation. Gland Pharma collaboration adds an asset-light sterile-API platform.
leadership: FY26 revenue ₹2,023 Cr (+37% YoY), OPM 29%, PAT ₹364 Cr (+40%); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹642 Cr (+119% YoY), EBITDA ₹231 Cr (35.5%), PAT ₹147 Cr vs ₹14 Cr; ROCE 26.5%, ROE 21%. Working-capital days cut to 84 from 137. Serves global innovator pharma on ~3 large commercial CMS molecules with 5-6 year visibility; ₹1,460 Cr capex programme (₹870 Cr spent). Mkt cap ~₹29,000 Cr.
non_rep: CDMO relationships with innovators take 3-5 years to establish (tech transfer, audits, regulatory filings) and Neuland's 5-10 year relationships are now scaling to ₹500-1,000 Cr-size molecules. Peptide synthesis capability for GLP-1-class molecules is rare globally — only a handful of manufacturers have it — and complex-chemistry plus sterile-API capability (via Gland) is harder still to assemble.
tailwinds: GLP-1 peptide API demand (obesity/diabetes drugs) — peptide plant commissioning Sep-2026
China+1 API sourcing by global pharma
CDMO outsourcing trend from innovators; 1 new commercial molecule in FY27, 1-2 in FY28
Management aspiration of ~20% annual growth in FY27-28 with 25%+ long-term EBITDA margin
risks: Customer/molecule concentration — ~3 commercial CMS molecules drive most revenue (management, 5 Aug 2026)
CDMO lumpiness: quarterly OPM swung 12% to 40% across FY26-Q1 FY27
GLP-1 capacity race — Lonza, Samsung Bio and Indian peers investing heavily
Regulatory inspection risk (US FDA) — new peptide facility still to be inspected
ROCE dilution from ₹1,460 Cr capex cycle (FY26 FCF -₹50 Cr, borrowings ₹301 Cr)
track: CMS revenue growth and commercialisation of the pipeline molecule guided for FY27
Peptide facility qualification, FDA inspection and Module 1 utilisation

(Japan) for aluminium paste; AVL Metal Powders (Belgium) export partnership. Customers include UltraTech, Shree Cement, UPL, Solar Industries, Sumitomo Chemical, Sun Pharma, Aurobindo.
leadership: FY26 consolidated revenue ₹824 Cr (+19% YoY), OPM 8%, PAT ₹31 Cr (-21%, hit by the ₹17.29 Cr exceptional loss from the 11-Apr-2025 Umred plant fire); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹233 Cr (+27%), EBITDA ₹20.8 Cr (9%), PAT ₹13.7 Cr vs -₹5.4 Cr — powders ₹154 Cr, foils ₹60 Cr, conductors ₹17 Cr. name: NLC India Limited
moat: Navratna PSU lignite/coal miner and regulated power generator: captive lignite mines (Neyveli, Barsingsar) and Talabira coal give fuel-cost security, and CERC-regulated tariffs give assured returns on a regulated equity base (₹12,464 Cr, targeted ₹19,679 Cr by 2030). Installed thermal capacity ~5,960 MW after the 1,980 MW Ghatampur (NUPPL) project reached full COD on 13-Jun-2026, plus ~1,734 MW renewables. FY26 revenue ₹17,490 Cr (+14%), OPM 32%, PAT ₹3,769 Cr (+39%).
leadership: India's only significant lignite-based generator and a growing coal producer (Q1 FY27 coal 40.85 lakh t, +7.8%); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹4,717 Cr (+23%), EBITDA ₹1,471 Cr (+57%, 31.2%), reported PAT ₹436 Cr (-48% on lower regulatory deferral income and tax normalisation); group generation 8,262 MU (+25%), power-debtor collection 100%. 'NLCIL at 2030': mining 50 → 104 MTPA, thermal 5,960 → 10,020 MW, RE 1,734 → 10,110 MW with ₹1.16 lakh Cr capex FY26-30. CRISIL AAA/Stable reaffirmed 2-Sep-2026.
non_rep: Multi-decade mining leases, sovereign ownership (69.47% after the Jun-2026 OFS), AAA funding cost and a regulated-return model cannot be replicated by private entrants; renewable assets (708.96 MW + 4 MW green hydrogen) are being housed in subsidiary NIRL to unlock value. The same PSU status slows execution and keeps the business tied to a polluting fuel.

Regulated-equity expansion (₹12,464 Cr → ₹19,679 Cr by 2030) and Talabira coal/thermal build-out

name: Power Finance Corporation Limited
moat: India's largest power-sector infrastructure financier (Maharatna, RBI-registered IFC) with a consolidated loan book of ₹11.60 lakh Cr (30-Jun-2026) including 52.6%-owned REC; sovereign backing gives AAA funding (CRISIL AAA/Stable reaffirmed 05-Aug-2026). Boards approved REC's merger into PFC on 28-Jun-2026 (88 PFC shares per 100 REC, appointed date 01-Apr-2027), which will make it a single ₹11 lakh Cr+ Government power lender. Moat is narrow: scale and quasi-sovereign cost of funds, but spreads are being competed down to a 2.40-2.50% FY27 guide.
leadership: #1 power-sector financier alongside subsidiary REC and India's largest renewable financier (RE book ₹1.63 lakh Cr, Jun-26). FY26 consolidated revenue ₹1,15,450 Cr (+8%), PAT ₹33,625 Cr (+10%), EPS ₹78.49, ROE 21%; standalone FY26 PAT ₹20,051 Cr (+16%). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26, results 07-Aug-2026) consolidated PAT ₹8,998 Cr (flat YoY), financing margin 39%, GNPA 0.66% (vs 1.47% Jun-25), NNPA 0.13%, standalone CRAR 23.35%; FY26 sanctions ₹2.85 lakh Cr, disbursements ₹1.65 lakh Cr.
non_rep: Government ownership (55.99%) and Maharatna status give access to low-cost domestic bond and foreign-currency borrowings (~60% bonds / 20% bank / 20% FX, 65% fixed-rate) that private lenders cannot match at ₹10 lakh Cr scale; decades-long relationships with state DISCOMs, gencos and central utilities plus a mandated role in Govt schemes (RDSS, smart metering) and a ₹2.5-3 lakh Cr sanctioned-but-undisbursed pipeline are not replicable by a new entrant.

moat: Navratna PSU (GoI + Himachal Govt 81.85%) — hydro, thermal, solar, wind. name: HEG Limited
moat: One of ~6 global players in UHP graphite electrodes, running the world's largest single-site plant (1,00,000 t/yr, >90% utilised in Q1 FY27 vs Western peers at 60-65%; 1,15,000 t by early FY28) with large-diameter machining and ~65-70% exports to 30 countries. Composite scheme effective 01-Sep-2026 (record date 07-Sep-2026, 1:1): electrodes demerge into separately listed HEG Graphite (to be renamed HEG) while the existing listed entity, renamed HEG Advanced Materials (02-Sep-2026), keeps the 20,000 t graphite-anode project, battery energy solutions, green power and the merged Bhilwara Energy 300 MW debt-free hydro (8 HEG shares per 7 BEL shares). Moat is narrow: cost/scale and know-how, not pricing power.
leadership: India's largest graphite electrode exporter; stake in GrafTech International (NYSE). FY26 consolidated sales ₹2,568 Cr (+19%), OPM 16%, PAT ₹341 Cr (vs ₹115 Cr FY25), other income ₹259 Cr; Q4 FY26 (Mar-26) was a loss of ₹114 Cr on a ₹126 Cr standalone EBITDA loss. Q1 FY27 (Jun-26, call 22-Jul-2026) standalone revenue ₹681 Cr (+11%), EBITDA ₹211 Cr (+38%, margin 29% vs 23%), consolidated PAT ₹122 Cr (+23%); treasury ₹858 Cr, standalone debt-free. FY27 guide: 90-95% utilisation, 28-29% EBITDA margin, 5-10% price hikes from Q3 FY27; anode plant commercial production Q1 FY28 (₹2,200-2,300 Cr, 40% spent).
non_rep: UHP electrode production requires specialised graphitisation and needle-coke know-how — capital-intensive with a 2-3-year build and a 50-year global oligopoly (HEG the last new entrant, 1976); needle coke supply is controlled by a few global suppliers. The anode plant (20,000 t, expandable to 30,000 t for ₹3,100 Cr total, ₹1,240 Cr SBI debt tied up) leverages the same carbon/graphitisation skills, and ~70% of capacity is being tied into 3-5-year tier-1 contracts.

Listing of HEG Graphite after 07-Sep-2026 record date; which entity the portfolio holds; US final AD/CVD ruling (end-Sep-2026)

name: Ingersoll-Rand (India) Limited
moat: 75%-owned India subsidiary of Ingersoll Rand Inc. (NYSE: IR). Manufactures and services industrial air compressors (single 'Air Solutions' segment) under Ingersoll Rand, Gardner Denver, CompAir, NASH, ARO and Milton Roy brands; global parent supplies technology, brand premium and export access. Legacy plant runs at full 60,000 units/yr; the ₹170 Cr Sanand (Gujarat) facility (24,000 units phase-1, engineered-to-order centrifugal/gas/reciprocating compressors) was inaugurated 14-Oct-2025 and declared fully operational with commercial production at the 14-Aug-2026 AGM, lifting capacity 1.5x by 2028.
leadership: Premium compressed-air brand in India with ROCE 57% and ROE 43% (FY26), debt-free. FY26 sales ₹1,392 Cr (+4%), OPM 24% (FY25 26%), PAT ₹256 Cr (-4%), EPS ₹81.10, final dividend ₹20/share (25% payout after 94-99% payouts in FY24-FY25). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26, results 13-Aug-2026) sales ₹379 Cr (+20% YoY), OPM 24%, PAT ₹70 Cr (+19%), EPS ₹22.32; FY26 CFO ₹274 Cr vs PAT ₹256 Cr, FCF ₹196 Cr after ₹78 Cr Sanand capex.
non_rep: Century-long India presence, parent technology (centrifugal, oil-free, engineered compressors) and a large installed base feeding service/aftermarket revenue create customer stickiness; a 75% MNC parent with global sourcing and export routes (Sanand positioned for exports) is hard for domestic rivals to copy. Brand premium sustains 24-26% OPM versus low-teens for most local compressor makers.

name: Welspun Corp Limited
moat: India's only large-diameter line-pipe maker with both SAW and ERW capability plus US manufacturing (Little Rock, Arkansas; new HFIW ERW mill commissioned Q1 FY27, LSAW line due by end-FY27) and a Saudi footprint via >22%-owned associate EPIC (largest shareholder, 15-year presence). Also DI pipes, TMT/billets, stainless pipes & bars (Welspun Specialty) and Sintex water tanks/plastic pipes. Serves oil & gas, LNG, water, hydrogen, nuclear and defence across 50+ countries; record global order book ~₹24,750 Cr (22-Jul-2026), US booked through FY28.
leadership: One of the largest global line-pipe producers. FY26 revenue ₹16,770 Cr (+20%), EBITDA ₹2,236 Cr (+33%), OPM 13%, PAT ₹1,620 Cr (FY25 ₹1,902 Cr had ₹1,248 Cr other income), ROCE 23%, ROE 19%; PBILDT/tonne ₹14,413 vs ₹11,922 (CARE, 05-Aug-2026). Q1 FY27 (Jun-26, results 24-Jul-2026): revenue ₹4,081 Cr (+15%), record EBITDA ₹756 Cr (+35%, margin 18.5% vs 15.8%), PAT ₹1,046 Cr incl. ₹548 Cr gain on 4.5% EPIC stake sale (₹499 Cr ex-exceptional, +42%); net cash ₹2,336 Cr after ₹834 Cr quarterly capex. FY26 revenue ₹2,940 Cr (+7%), OPM 35%, PAT ₹657 Cr (FY25 ₹770 Cr included a Mashobra one-off), ROCE 21%, CFO ₹993 Cr; Q1 FY27 (12 Aug 2026) revenue ₹698 Cr (+15%), EBITDA ₹207 Cr (+6%, margin 29.7% vs 32.0%), PAT ₹120 Cr, RevPAR ₹12,801 (+12.8%). Pipeline: 30 new properties by 2031 (23 managed / 1,833 keys plus 7 owned incl. Oberoi Grand Delhi Sep-2028, Kolkata 2029, Hebbal Bengaluru mixed-use, Goa 2029).
non_rep: Luxury hospitality moats are built from decades of service culture, iconic assets and customer trust. Replacement cost is enormous — irreplaceable sites such as Oberoi Mumbai, Trident Nariman Point (585 keys), Udaivilas or Rajvilas — and brand replication is even harder; Trident RevPAR +13.8% vs upper-upscale segment +9.2% in Q1 FY27 shows the premium persists even in a soft foreign-arrivals quarter.
tailwinds: Scarcity of top-end hospitality supply in premium markets
Growth in affluent domestic travel and MICE (Mumbai; BRICS summit and Air India show in Q2 FY27)
Asset-light expansion through management contracts (23 hotels / 1,833 keys) and 7 owned projects to 2031
Net-cash balance sheet funding ₹600-700 Cr p.a. capex without leverage
risks: Macro, geopolitical and travel downturns: foreign arrivals -10% in Q1 FY27 on the West Asia crisis (Oberoi RevPAR +8.2% vs luxury segment +13.2%)
Execution risk in pipeline ramp-up: Kolkata Oberoi Grand delayed to 2029 (from 2028), Rajgarh 3-year stabilisation, unquantified heritage-restoration costs
Margin compression from staff cost inflation (working-hours policy, labour codes), renovations and power/fuel costs (EBITDA margin -230 bps YoY in Q1 FY27)
Capital intensity rising: capex guidance lifted to ₹600-700 Cr p.a. (29 May 2026) from ₹400-500 Cr, incl. a 7.6 lakh sq ft retail component at Hebbal
track: ARR, RevPAR and occupancy across flagship hotels; Oberoi brand vs luxury-segment RevPAR gap
Pipeline conversion: Oberoi Grand Delhi (Sep-2028), Kolkata (2029), Hebbal, Goa; Wildflower Hall lease bid (qualifying bids 10 Sep 2026)
EBITDA margin recovery toward 32%+ as Rajgarh ramps and renovations complete (H2 FY27)
Cash generation vs the ₹600-700 Cr annual capex; dividend payout (15% in FY26)

Moved comp.growth 3.5 to 4.0 on RevPAR +12.8% and revenue +15%. Self peer score 8.0 to 7.9. name: Kamdhenu Limited
moat: Kamdhenu has an asset-light distribution-and-brand moat rather than a manufacturing moat: 100+ franchisee rolling mills (52.5 lakh TPA) make TMT, structural steel and colour-coated sheets under the Kamdhenu brand and pay a fixed royalty (~₹450-470/t), sold through 12,500+ dealers and 500+ distributors. Royalty income reached ₹174 Cr in FY26 (+25%) and a record ₹48.1 Cr in Q1 FY27 (Jun-26, +16%), now the bulk of profit. The paints business sits in separately listed Kamdhenu Ventures.
leadership: India's largest retail TMT brand: brand sales turnover ~₹23,000 Cr in FY26, franchisee volumes 37.9 lakh MT (+10%), own Bhiwadi plant 1.21 lakh MT. FY26 revenue ₹763 Cr (+2%), PBILDT margin 13.3% vs 10.2%, PAT ₹78 Cr (+28%), ROCE 29%, ROE 22%; Q1 FY27 (29 Jul 2026) revenue ₹213 Cr (+9%), PBT ₹36.4 Cr (+27%), PAT ₹28.7 Cr (+34%), franchise volumes 10.3 lakh MT (+9%). Debt-free with ₹258 Cr cash and liquid investments (Mar-26); CARE upgraded issuer rating to A+ (Stable) on 29 Jun 2026.
non_rep: Brand trust in construction materials matters because builders and retailers de-risk with familiar names; a franchise network of 100+ mills plus 12,500 dealers compounds reach and convenience and cannot be assembled quickly. The moat is moderated because TMT is largely commoditised (own-plant realisations fell to ₹48,507/t in FY26 from ₹50,622) and integrated majors (Tata Tiscon, JSW Neosteel) compete for the same retail shelf.
tailwinds: Housing and infrastructure demand driving TMT consumption
Shift from unorganised to branded building materials (franchise volumes +10% FY26, +9% Q1 FY27)
Royalty-led margin expansion and geographic push into Southern India
Captive 5 MWp solar plant (commissioned Jun-2026) saving ₹4-5 Cr p.a.
risks: Commodity-linked volatility in steel spreads (own-manufacturing segment is a price-taker)
Heavy competition from larger integrated steel brands in retail TMT
Brand salience can fade if franchise execution or quality control weakens
Low headline growth (FY26 revenue +2%) and a large idle treasury (₹258 Cr) with only 14% payout
track: Brand sales turnover, royalty income per tonne and franchisee count (CARE trigger: royalty below ₹140 Cr)
Franchise additions and dealer productivity, especially South India
Own-plant OPM and utilisation vs TMT price; deployment of the ₹258 Cr treasury (capex, dividends, buyback)

name: GAUDIUM IVF N WOMEN H L
moat: A trust-and-outcomes moat in a highly personal healthcare category: fertility chains create stickiness through clinician reputation, counselling, success rates (Gaudium cites 58% clinical pregnancy rate, 62% first-attempt, 25-30% international patients) and referral flywheels. Narrower than a hospital moat and, at 8 hubs / 28 spokes, still sub-scale versus Indira or Nova; the moat is being tested by a 10-hub rollout in FY27 that compressed EBITDA margin to 12.5% in Q1 FY27 (Jun-26).
leadership: India's first listed pure-play fertility chain (mainboard IPO 20-24 Feb 2026 at ₹79; listed 27 Feb 2026): hub-and-spoke network of 8 hubs and 28 spokes, a 15-bed day-care hospital (Janakpuri) and an in-house pharmacy. FY26 revenue ₹104.35 Cr (+47.6%), EBITDA margin 36% (FY25 41%), PAT ₹24.5 Cr (+28%), ROE 25%. Q1 FY27 (14 Aug 2026) revenue ₹19.4 Cr (+9.1%), EBITDA ₹2.4 Cr (12.5% vs 29%), PAT ₹1.8 Cr (-42%). Market cap ~₹870 Cr.
non_rep: Patients choose fertility providers on trust, clinician quality and perceived success probability, so mature centres are hard to dislodge; Gaudium's SOP-driven, non-star-doctor model and first-in-India AI embryology tools (Sid and Erica, ~8% first-attempt uplift in early data) are its attempt to make outcomes replicable across new hubs. The replicability itself is unproven — new hubs are guided to break even in 3-6 months but only one of ten FY27 hubs was open by mid-July 2026.
tailwinds: Low fertility-treatment penetration in India
Rising acceptance of assisted reproductive care; ART Act formalisation favouring organised chains
Network expansion: 10 new hubs in FY27 (₹2.5 Cr each) funded by IPO proceeds; South Extension opened 16 Jul 2026, Gurgaon and Nagpur next
AI-embryology differentiation and international patient flow (25-30% of mix)
risks: Doctor dependency and centre-level execution variability
Growth deceleration and margin collapse: Q1 FY27 revenue +9% vs FY26 +48%, EBITDA margin 12.5% vs 29%
Weak cash conversion: debtor days 187 (FY26), CFO ₹7 Cr vs PAT ₹24 Cr; working-capital days 40 to 91
Scope creep post-IPO (₹15 Cr Lucknow women's hospital, international spokes in Paris/Nigeria/Sydney) and a short listed history
Reputational damage from weak clinical outcomes
track: Q2-Q4 FY27 rebound to the ~30% growth / 27-29% margin guidance; hub openings vs the 10-hub plan
Receivables (187 debtor days) and CFO/PAT conversion in H1 FY27 results
New-hub break-even (guided 3-6 months) and doctor/embryologist retention
IPO-proceeds utilisation reports and any deviation

name: Motilal Oswal NASDAQ 100 ETF
moat: Again, not a business moat in the classic sense. The edge lies in scale, familiarity, liquidity and ease of access for Indian investors wanting broad Nasdaq-100 exposure through an onshore listed vehicle.
leadership: The official fund page cites AUM of about Rs 10,971.5 crore as of 31 March 2026, TER of 0.59%, tracking error of 0.73% and a long operating history going back to March 2011.
non_rep: Compared with smaller wrappers, scale can help liquidity, tighter spreads and investor comfort. But the product itself remains replicable and ultimate returns depend on underlying Nasdaq constituents, not franchise economics.
tailwinds: Long-duration secular growth in technology, software and semis
Rupee weakness versus the dollar
Retail demand for simple international equity exposure
risks: High concentration in US growth and tech factors
Tracking error and temporary liquidity gaps
Sharp valuation drawdowns in the Nasdaq complex
track: AUM and on-exchange liquidity
Tracking error / tracking difference
Underlying earnings momentum of top Nasdaq holdings

name: Suzlon Energy Limited
moat: India's largest wind OEM (~30-35% of the ~50 GW installed base per ICRA) with a scale-and-platform moat: the S144 turbine is 88% of a record ~6.1 GW order book (Jun-26), 80%+ local sourcing, an integrated WTG + EPC + DevCo model and a 15 GW+ O&M annuity (RE AMS Q1 FY27 revenue ₹526 Cr, EBITDA margin 43%). FY26 revenue ₹16,679 Cr (+54%), EBITDA ₹3,022 Cr (18.1%), PAT ₹3,163 Cr (incl. deferred-tax credits; PBT ₹2,422 Cr), deliveries 2,456 MW. ICRA A+ (Stable)/A1 (limits revised 19 May 2026). Walker Chandiok unmodified FY26 audit opinion.

Industry demand of 8-9 GW in FY27 and ~10 GW in FY28; FDRE tenders need wind
Record ~6.1 GW order book, 84% PSU and C&I, giving multi-year revenue visibility
Repowering of India's aging wind fleet and 1.2 GW NTPC Gujarat project execution
European re-entry with S175/S163 platforms (S163 6.x MW slated H1 2027)

Margin pressure from EPC mix and West Asia logistics: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.6% vs 19.2%, WTG contribution margin 23.4% vs 26%; FY27 guide 17-18%
Finance costs rising (₹134 Cr in Q1 FY27 vs ₹103 Cr) despite net cash; FY26 finance cost ₹462 Cr vs ~₹250 Cr guided
FY26 PAT flattered by ₹741 Cr net deferred-tax credits (tax rate -31%); normalised tax from FY27 (22% in Q1)
Legacy promoter governance overhang; promoter holding only 11.70%

Trade receivable days, inventory and commissioning vs deliveries (1,257 MW erected backlog)

Finance-cost run-rate and net cash trajectory (₹2,322 Cr at Jun-26)

name: HLE Glascoat Limited
moat: Specialised chemical/pharma process-equipment franchise: India's leading agitated nutsche filter-dryer (filtration & drying) brand, #2 domestic glass-lined equipment maker, plus Thaletec (Germany, glass-lined, US/EU), Kinam (70%, heat exchangers; amalgamation NCLT-approved 14 Aug 2025) and Omeras/HLE Surface Technologies GmbH (surface enamelling, consolidated from Aug 2025). European cross-sell via Thaletec/Omeras; Omeras order book ~₹78 Cr (May-26) and glass-fused-to-steel entry into biogas/wastewater

name: Cyient Limited
moat: Engineering R&D (ER&D) and geospatial/network services (DET segment, ~75% of group revenue) with decades-long embedded relationships in aerospace, rail and communications, plus Cyient DLM (listed electronics manufacturing) and Cyient Semiconductors (custom power ASSPs; Kinetic Technologies acquired, valued at $500 mn post-money in the May-2026 Edelweiss round). Domain-heavy, certification-gated design work is sticky, but growth has stalled: FY26 revenue ₹7,268 Cr (-1%), OPM 12%, PAT ₹463 Cr (-29%); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) group revenue ₹2,076 Cr (+21% YoY incl. Kinetic), DET revenue ₹1,540 Cr ($162.5 mn, cc -0.9% YoY), DET EBIT 13.2%, group PAT ₹104 Cr.
leadership: Mid-tier Indian ER&D leader (300+ customers, 15,000+ associates, 30+ countries) with strong aerospace, rail and geospatial franchises; founder-led (BVR Mohan Reddy; son Krishna Bodanapu Executive Vice Chairman & MD, CEO Sukamal Banerjee). Near debt-free (borrowings ₹431 Cr), FY26 CFO ₹787 Cr vs PAT ₹463 Cr, FCF ₹693 Cr, ₹720 Cr buyback at ₹1,125 completed Jul-26, payout 42%; but ROCE 12.3% and ROE 8.6% (17%/13% earlier). Market cap ~₹12,400 Cr at ₹1,116 (P/E 30).
non_rep: Aerospace/rail engineering carries high certification and switching barriers; multi-year design and aftermarket/MRO programmes lock in vendors across the product lifecycle (Transportation & Mobility grew 14.8% YoY cc in Q1 FY27, fifth straight quarter of growth), and the geospatial/utility network data assets are hard to rebuild.
tailwinds: Global ER&D outsourcing ($80-100 bn market) and lifecycle-engineering/MRO shift ('Nothing Less' strategy, Investor Day 25 Aug 2026)
Aerospace, rail and automotive recovery: Transportation & Mobility +14.8% YoY cc in Q1 FY27
Large-deal engine: 5 large deals in Q4 FY26-Q1 FY27, 9 new qualified deals adding $300 mn+ pipeline, highest pipeline in 12 quarters
TAO Digital Solutions acquisition ($40-50 mn revenue; CCI approval 25 Aug 2026) adds data/AI software engineering
Semiconductor optionality: organic revenue +5% QoQ for five quarters, $100 mn+ pipeline, India GaN/power push
risks: DET growth stalled: cc revenue -0.5% QoQ / -0.9% YoY in Q1 FY27; mid-single-digit FY27 growth aim now 'very hard' (23 Jul 2026)
15% DET EBIT exit target for Q4 FY27 pushed out; FY26 PAT -29%, ROE 8.6%
Energy/strategic-unit contraction (-8.2% QoQ), aerospace flying-hours concerns and delayed connectivity decisions
Semiconductor cash burn (EBIT loss ₹28 Cr in Q1 FY27, ~$3 mn/quarter to cover) and rising USD acquisition debt (Kinetic, TAO)
Wage inflation, attrition and client concentration in aerospace/communications
track: DET constant-currency growth returning in H2 FY27 and order intake (+5.3% YoY in Q1)
DET EBIT trajectory toward 15% (13.2% in Q1 FY27) after TAO consolidation
TAO Digital closing/integration and group debt after the USD-funded acquisitions
Semiconductor segment losses and path to break-even; Cyient DLM order book
change_remark: Execution pillar 6 to 5.5, red_flags.business 6 to 5.5, comp.growth 6 to 5, comp.mgmt 8 to 7.5, q 6.6 to 6.3: Q1 FY27 (23 Jul 2026) DET constant-currency revenue fell 0.9% YoY, management said the mid-single-digit FY27 growth aim is now 'very hard' and pushed out the 15% EBIT exit target; FY26 PAT -29%. Ownership_behaviour 7 to 7.5 as promoters/KMP abstained from the ₹720 Cr buyback at ₹1,125 completed Jul-2026 (holding up to 24.70%). Positives: DET EBIT 13.2% (+79 bps), order intake +5.3%, TAO Digital CCI approval and Investor Day 25 Aug 2026. Conviction 6, HOLD unchanged.

name: AGI Greenpac Limited
moat: One of India's two largest container-glass makers (AGI Glaspac, 2,100 TPD across three plants; 91% of revenue) with security caps & closures (AGI Closures), PET/HDPE bottles (AGI Plastek) and a growing specialty/premium glass line; glass containers serve alcoholic beverages (75%), food & beverages (18%) and pharma (7%), value-added products ~25% of FY26 revenue. FY26 revenue ₹2,665 Cr (+5%), OPM 22%, PAT ₹352 Cr (+9%); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹785 Cr (+14.2%), EBITDA ₹175 Cr (+23.1%, margin 22.3%), PAT ₹99 Cr (+11.8%). Capital-intensive furnaces, premium-glass approvals and closures capability differentiate an otherwise cyclical, energy-heavy industry.
leadership: Top-2 Indian container-glass producer (Somany/HSIL lineage, Sandip Somany CMD) with ROCE 19.6%, ROE 15.8%, 5-yr profit CAGR 32%; deleveraged to borrowings ₹241 Cr (Mar-26, from ₹553 Cr; net debt/EBITDA 0.11x). Capacity to rise to 2,600 TPD by Mar-2027 via a fourth, 500 TPD greenfield plant for North/Central India, plus a new aluminium-cans foray (1.6 bn cans). The contested HNG acquisition is effectively lost to INSCO (SC Jan-2025; CCI dismissals 15 Jul 2025 and 20 Apr 2026). Market cap ~₹4,800 Cr at ₹740 (P/E 13; -14% over 1 year).
non_rep: Glass furnaces are capital- and energy-intensive with multi-year build times and location-bound logistics; premium/specialty glass approvals (spirits, perfume, pharma vials), a dedicated glass R&D and decoration centre and anti-counterfeit closures create moderate switching friction with liquor and beverage majors.
tailwinds: Premiumisation of spirits/beer and beauty packaging (value-added ~25% of revenue)
Food, beverage and pharma glass-packaging demand; sustainability shift to recyclable glass
Capacity-led growth: 2,100 to 2,600 TPD by Mar-2027 (fourth plant, North/Central India)
Rigid-packaging diversification: closures, PET and the new aluminium-cans entry
Deleveraged balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.11x) funding organic expansion
risks: Energy and soda-ash cost cyclicality (West Asia escalation pressured Q1 FY27 costs)
High capital intensity: 500 TPD greenfield plant and aluminium cans (no disclosed project cost/returns yet)
Alcoholic beverages 75% of glass revenue - regulatory/excise and demand concentration
HNG revived under INSCO ownership adds competitive capacity; AGI's consolidation thesis is dead
Low dividend payout (13-14%) and thin institutional ownership (FII 6.3%, DII 1.1%)
track: Specialty/premium glass and value-added revenue mix (target above 25%)
EBITDA margin (22.3% in Q1 FY27) vs energy cost per tonne
Greenfield 500 TPD plant and aluminium-cans project: capex, timelines and funding
Capacity utilisation as 2,600 TPD comes online by Mar-2027
change_remark: Capital_allocation 6 to 6.5, execution 6 to 6.5, red_flags.financial 6 to 7, comp.capital 6 to 6.5, q 6.3 to 6.4, self peer score 6.8 to 6.9. Drivers: borrowings fell to ₹241 Cr at Mar-26 from ₹553 Cr (net debt/EBITDA 0.11x), Q1 FY27 (28 Jul 2026) revenue ₹785 Cr (+14.2%) with EBITDA ₹175 Cr (+23.1%, margin 22.3%) despite West Asia energy costs, and the contested HNG bet is effectively closed after the CCI's second dismissal on 20 Apr 2026, replaced by organic expansion to 2,600 TPD by Mar-2027. Promoter 60.39% stable. Conviction 6, HOLD unchanged; Jul-2026 concall transcript not reachable.

name: Asahi India Glass Limited
moat: India's largest integrated glass company and the dominant automotive-glass supplier (~70% passenger-car OEM share, gaining further in FY27) with decades-long approvals at Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai and others, plus a large architectural/float-glass business now enlarged by the new Soniyana (Chittorgarh) float line. Backed by AGC (Japan, 21.2%) technology and a Maruti Suzuki shareholding. FY26 revenue ₹4,982 Cr (+8%), OPM 18%, PAT ₹345 Cr (-6% on higher depreciation/interest from the float capex); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹1,413 Cr (+15%), EBITDA margin 23.0% (+733 bps), PAT ₹149 Cr (+165%), float-glass EBIT margin 21.5% (9.5%), auto-glass EBIT margin 13.5% (+288 bps).
leadership: #1 in Indian auto glass with an entrenched OEM position; sand-to-solutions integration (float, processing, fabrication, AIS Windows retail) and a growing architectural/consumer franchise. ₹1,000 Cr QIP at ₹844.79 (Sep-2025, 24 QIBs) cut borrowings to ₹2,198 Cr (Mar-26, from ₹2,696 Cr) and finance cost by 21% YoY in Q1 FY27; ROCE 11.5%, ROE 10.3% (depressed by the capex phase), 5-yr sales CAGR 16%. Market cap ~₹24,600 Cr at ₹964 (P/E 55; +18% over 1 year).
non_rep: Auto glass is a certification-gated, model-life-locked business; OEM co-development, single/dual-source approvals for laminated/tempered glass, AGC technology and captive float integration are extremely hard to replicate, and the new float capacity raises the entry bar in architectural glass.
tailwinds: Auto production growth and glass premiumisation (larger, laminated, acoustic, solar-control glass; PV share gains in Q1 FY27)
Architectural/float glass and construction demand absorbing the new Soniyana float capacity
Raw-material relief: material cost 25.5% of revenue in Q1 FY27 vs 37.4% (soda ash, energy)
Value-added glass mix and AIS Windows consumer channel
China+1 / import substitution in float glass (anti-dumping regime)
risks: Auto-cycle cyclicality and OEM concentration (Maruti Suzuki the largest customer)
Leverage still meaningful: borrowings ₹2,198 Cr, FY26 FCF -₹139 Cr (third negative year), inventory days 302
Energy costs (power & fuel +30% YoY in Q1 FY27) and soda-ash price reversal
Rich valuation (P/E ~55, 6.2x book) on ROE of ~10%
Promoter (Sanjay Labroo) pledge of 42 lakh shares (1.65% of capital) for personal borrowing
track: Auto vs architectural mix and float-glass EBIT margin sustainability (21.5% in Q1 FY27)

Conviction 7, HOLD unchanged; no earnings calls held.

name: M M Forgings Limited
moat: Chennai-based maker of steel forgings and machined components (crankshafts, front-axle beams, connecting rods, chassis parts) for commercial vehicles, tractors, passenger cars and off-highway, with a large export franchise (US/Europe) and a rising machined share (67% of Q1 FY27 sales after ~₹625 Cr of machining capex in five years). Scale forging capacity plus in-house machining and long OEM relationships give a mid-tier cost/quality edge. FY26 revenue ₹1,590 Cr (+4%), OPM 18%, PAT ₹99 Cr (-20%); Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) net sales ₹427 Cr (+16%), EBITDA ₹75 Cr (18%), reported PAT ₹90 Cr including a ₹56 Cr net gain on the Oragadam land sale (PBT +30% ex-exceptional).
leadership: Among India's larger CV/off-highway forging exporters (78,000 t sold in FY26; guiding >90,000 t in FY27 and 1,00,000-1,10,000 t in FY28) with integrated forging + machining, a 16,500-t heavy press due in Q4 FY27 and an EV-motor subsidiary (Abhinava Rizel) at first-order/SOP stage. Leveraged capex phase: borrowings ₹1,235 Cr at Mar-26 (management's gross debt ~₹750-800 Cr), interest ₹78 Cr in FY26, ROCE 9%, ROE 10.5%; market cap ~₹3,100 Cr at ₹642 (P/E 28 on TTM PAT inflated by the land gain; +102% in 1 year).
non_rep: Forging dies, metallurgical process control and multi-year OEM/Tier-1 approvals for safety-critical drivetrain parts create switching friction; the growing machined (value-added) mix and heavy-press capability raise the bar for smaller Indian forgers as US/European OEMs relocate procurement to low-cost countries, though the product remains cyclical and competitive.
tailwinds: Global CV and off-highway recovery: US CV strength and India CV/tractor/PV improvement cited for Q1 FY27
Export / China+1 and European forge closures shifting procurement to India
Machining value-addition (67% mix; realisation ₹2.02 lakh/t, +4.7% QoQ) and EBITDA-margin target of 20%+
Capacity: 4,000-t press commissioned Q2 FY27, 16,500-t press in Q4 FY27; FY30 revenue aspiration ₹3,000 Cr
EV-agnostic components plus Abhinava Rizel EV motors (first commercial order, SOP under way)
risks: Deep CV-cycle cyclicality; FY26 PAT -20% as interest (₹78 Cr) and depreciation (₹103 Cr) rose
Leverage: borrowings ₹1,235 Cr (Mar-26), ROCE 9%; debt to stay ₹750-800 Cr (management) through ₹150 Cr FY27 capex
Export and customer concentration; freight/geopolitics (Strait of Hormuz disruption added ₹4 Cr freight in Q1 FY27)

Gross debt (₹750-800 Cr) and interest cover as the 16,500-t press is capitalised

name: Sundram Fasteners Limited
moat: TVS-group maker of high-tensile fasteners, powertrain and cold-extruded/forged components, water pumps and sintered parts for global OEMs (GM, Stellantis, Cummins, Class-8 truck makers, Hyundai/KIA) with ~30% export share and subsidiaries in the UK and China. The moat is decades-long OEM qualification, pass-through steel contracts with domestic OEMs, and a diversification engine (wind-energy fasteners ₹350 Cr run-rate, aerospace with HAL/ISRO/GE/Skyroot, EV parts for GM and Stellantis) that peers of similar size lack.
leadership: FY26 consolidated: sales ₹6,289 Cr (+6%), OPM 16%, PAT ₹593 Cr (+9%), CFO ₹837 Cr, borrowings cut to ₹625 Cr. Q1 FY27 (results 4 Aug 2026): sales ₹1,846 Cr (+20% YoY), tonnage +13%, OPM 16%, PAT ₹169 Cr (+14%); FY27 guidance (6 Aug 2026 call) ~20% revenue growth, EBITDA margin exit ~16.5%, capex ~₹400 Cr, EV revenue ₹200-250 Cr, aerospace ₹100+ Cr. Ten-year ROE 18%, dividend payout ~28% every year.
non_rep: Metallurgy, cold-forging know-how and OEM approvals built since 1966 plus Nadcap/AS9100 aerospace accreditation cannot be bought quickly; ~₹400 Cr annual capex over three years and a ₹1,000 Cr+ new-project pipeline keep it ahead of domestic fastener rivals, though the product itself is not proprietary and margins have sat in a 15-18% band for a decade.
tailwinds: North American Class-8 truck upcycle: primary orders +20-25% YoY and backlogs at a 38-month high (Jun-2026) ahead of EPA 2027 norms
EV and hybrid programme ramp with GM and Stellantis: ₹200-250 Cr FY27 revenue from under ₹50 Cr in FY26, peak potential ₹750 Cr
Non-auto diversification - aerospace to ₹100+ Cr FY27 (₹500 Cr target in 2-3 years), wind fasteners to ₹500 Cr run-rate, Hyundai/KIA localisation under BIS/QCO
Domestic CV, PV and tractor demand growth matched in Q1 FY27 (M&HCV ~20%, PV ~23%, tractors 14-15%)
risks: Input-cost inflation from the West Asia conflict (steel, LPG/gas) with a lag on indirect-material compensation - EBITDA margin slipped to 16.1% in Q1 FY27
Auto cyclicality and a high H2 FY26 base; a reversal of the US truck pre-buy or INR appreciation would hit ~30% export revenue
Working-capital creep: inventory days 147 to 175 and cash-conversion cycle 144 to 173 days between FY24 and FY26
Imported capex delays (West Asia logistics) could push out new-capacity commissioning
Valuation: 40.7x TTM earnings after an 18% one-year rally, against a decade of 12% sales CAGR
track: FY27 delivery vs ~20% revenue-growth guidance and the ~16.5% exit EBITDA margin after Q2 indirect-material settlements
EV (₹200-250 Cr) and aerospace (₹100+ Cr) revenue ramp; wind run-rate toward ₹500 Cr
Inventory and cash-conversion-cycle trend; ₹400 Cr FY27 capex funded from CFO
Promoter holding stability at 46.94% and any group-level changes

Long-term CRISIL rating not fetched. Conviction 7, HOLD.

name: SoftTech Engineers Limited
moat: Pune-based owner of niche architecture-engineering-construction (AEC) software - AutoDCR/CivitPLAN building-plan approval, PWIMS, OPTICON, BIMDCR, Civit suite - deployed with urban local bodies and state authorities across 18 states, with screener citing ~80% share in Indian plan-approval automation. Switching costs are high once a municipality's approval workflow runs on the platform, and the new eTDR Exchange (live with BMC Mumbai since Jun 2026) and Civit TWIN tools have no direct competitor per management; but the customer is government, scale is tiny (FY26 revenue ₹133 Cr) and margins after capitalised R&D are thin.
leadership: FY26 (consolidated): revenue ₹133 Cr (+39%), OPM 24%, PAT ₹5.3 Cr; order book ₹232 Cr at Mar-26 (1.74x revenue). Q1 FY27 (results 12 Aug 2026): consolidated revenue ₹33.3 Cr (+23%), EBITDA ₹9.1 Cr (27.2%), PAT ₹1.2 Cr (+5%); standalone revenue +25% with SaaS ₹10.0 Cr (+56%, 31% of revenue); confirmed orders ₹220 Cr, pipeline ₹490 Cr; wins include ODPS 3.0 Gujarat (₹20 Cr) and a first corporate order from Mitsubishi (₹1.2 Cr).
non_rep: Two decades of rule-engine content for building bye-laws across states and embedded municipal workflows (permits, works management) would take a new entrant years of tendering and rule-coding to replicate; CARE (21 Aug 2026) still calls the order book moderate and the scale modest, and top-five clients were ~44% of FY26 revenue.
tailwinds: Recurring mix rising: SaaS 31% of Q1 FY27 revenue (25% a year earlier), recurring revenue 41%
Order visibility: confirmed orders ₹220 Cr plus ₹490 Cr pipeline vs FY26 revenue ₹133 Cr
New transaction-fee platforms (eTDR Exchange live in Mumbai since Jun 2026; Maharashtra mandate, AP proposal) and Civit TWIN AI plan-clearance
Working-capital improvement: debtor days 212 (FY24) to 95 (FY26); CARE operating cycle 287 to 195 days
risks: Promoter holding collapsed from 40.44% (Sep-23) to 18.88% (Jun-26) with a 7.3% pledge seen at Mar-24; cause not confirmed in sources reviewed
Earnings quality: heavy capitalised development (fixed assets ₹50 Cr to ₹100 Cr FY24-FY26), D&A ₹23 Cr vs PAT ₹5 Cr in FY26, negative free cash flow every year since FY19
Government-tender dependence and slow collections; top-five clients ~44% of FY26 revenue; sizeable unbilled revenue (CARE, 21 Aug 2026)
Micro-cap (₹584 Cr) trading at 116x earnings and 3.3x book with ROE below 3%; no dividend since FY19; zero institutional holders
Company Secretary/Compliance Officer resigned 21 Aug 2026 (effective 16 Oct 2026)
track: Explanation and stabilisation of the 18.9% promoter holding; any new pledge or SAST disclosures
Conversion of the ₹220 Cr order book and SaaS share (target: sustained rise above 31%)

Replacement of the Company Secretary by 16 Oct 2026

Key calls: ownership_behaviour cut to 3.5 for the unexplained fall in promoter holding from 40% to 19% with a past pledge; capital allocation 4.5 for perpetual negative FCF from capitalised R&D; execution 6 on growth and order book. name: Signatureglobal (India) Limited
moat: Largest developer of affordable and lower-mid-income housing in Delhi NCR by units (screener: ~27% share in Gurugram), now pivoting to premium (Tonino Lamborghini Residences launched Q1 FY27 at over ₹22,000/sq ft, GDV over ₹4,000 Cr). The moat is a Gurugram land bank and approvals pipeline (~17 mn sq ft forthcoming) plus a low-cost execution model; brand pull in the premium segment is unproven.
leadership: FY26 (13 May 2026): revenue ₹2,596 Cr, pre-sales ₹8,220 Cr, PAT ₹1,095 Cr of which ₹1,267 Cr was an exceptional gain on the 50:50 RMZ joint venture (Gurugram Commercity); net debt cut 77% to ₹200 Cr. Q1 FY27 (6 Aug 2026): revenue ₹550 Cr, PAT -₹17 Cr, pre-sales ₹1,970 Cr (+25% QoQ, -25% YoY), collections ₹670 Cr (-28% YoY), realisation ₹17,093/sq ft, cash ₹2,522 Cr, net debt ₹390 Cr. FY27 guidance unchanged: launches ₹15,000 Cr, pre-sales ₹10,000 Cr, collections ₹5,000 Cr, revenue ₹5,000 Cr.
non_rep: Assembling contiguous Gurugram land parcels, securing Haryana approvals and delivering 30,000+ units since 2014 took a decade; but competitors (DLF, Godrej, M3M, Max Estates) are all active in the same micro-market, so the advantage is local scale rather than a durable franchise. Percentage-of-completion accounting means reported P&L lags sales by 2-3 years.
tailwinds: Delhi NCR residential prices +24% YoY in Q2 2026 and launches +10% YoY in H1 2026 (management, 6 Aug 2026 call)
Premium pivot lifting realisations (₹12,457/sq ft FY25 to ₹15,250 FY26 to ₹17,093 Q1 FY27)

Earnings quality: FY26 PAT almost entirely the ₹1,267 Cr exceptional JV gain; reported OPM -1.9% FY26 and -8% in Q1 FY27; screener flags possible interest capitalisation

name: Black Box Limited
moat: Global digital-infrastructure integrator (network and data-centre build-outs, connected workspaces, cybersecurity, technology products) serving Fortune-100 enterprises and hyperscalers across the US, Europe, India, APAC, Middle East and LATAM with ~3,600 staff. The moat is relationship- and execution-based rather than product-based: multi-year (24-36 month) hyperscale data-centre programmes and an order backlog of ~US$950 mn (+83% YoY, Q1 FY27) give visibility, but the business is a ~9% EBITDA-margin services model with pass-through hardware.
leadership: FY26 revenue ₹6,322 Cr (+6%), OPM 9%, PAT ₹218 Cr; Q1 FY27 (results 12 Aug 2026) record revenue ₹1,718 Cr (+24% YoY), OPM ~9%, PAT ₹56 Cr (+19%). FY27 guidance (13 Aug 2026 call): revenue ₹7,800-8,000 Cr (+23-27%), EBITDA ₹725-750 Cr, PAT ₹300-325 Cr, order bookings US$1.3-1.4 bn; long-term target US$2 bn revenue by FY30. Acquired 2S Inovacoes Tecnologicas (Brazil, ~₹500 Cr annualised revenue) effective 1 May 2026.
non_rep: Two decades of hyperscaler and Fortune-100 vendor qualifications, a global delivery footprint (US, UK, Brazil, Middle East, India) and OEM partnerships (Cisco networking, AV/KVM products) are hard for Indian IT-services peers to replicate quickly; however the moat is narrow because hyperscaler programmes are competitively bid and margins are thin (OPM 9% in FY26 vs 2.7% in FY15).
tailwinds: Hyperscale data-centre and AI-infrastructure capex cycle in the US (backlog US$950 mn, +83% YoY at Jun-2026)
FY27 guidance of 23-27% revenue growth with 9.3-9.4% EBITDA margin and 38-50% PAT growth
Margin expansion track record: OPM 4.3% (FY23) to 9% (FY26) through mix shift to higher-value integration
Inorganic expansion (2S Brazil, May 2026) and CRISIL outlook revised to Positive on 16 Jun 2026
risks: Weak cash conversion: FY25 CFO -₹88 Cr and FY26 CFO ₹84 Cr vs PAT ₹205/218 Cr; debtor days 35 to 67 in FY26

name: Ashapura Minechem Ltd
moat: No pricing moat — bauxite is a freight-sensitive commodity — but Ashapura owns scarce export infrastructure in Guinea (Boffa port expanded to 8 mtpa, GSM port going from 6 to 10 mtpa by Q4 FY27, a 20,000 tpd washing plant under an operate-and-transfer model) and is India's leading bentonite processor (>1 mn t grinding capacity) with bleaching-clay (50% JV Ashapura Perfoclay) and kaolin/white-minerals lines. Guinea contributed ~84% of Q1 FY27 turnover.
leadership: FY26 revenue ₹5,237 Cr (+91%), OPM 11%, PAT ₹416 Cr (+44%), ROCE 20.7%, ROE 28%; five-year PAT CAGR 43%. Q1 FY27 (call 19 Aug 2026) revenue ₹1,616 Cr (+19.2% YoY), EBITDA ₹188.9 Cr (flat; margin 11.7% vs 13.8%), EPS ₹12.07; Guinea bauxite volume 2.34 mn t (2.05 mn t YoY; 3.16 mn t in Q4 FY26) at EBITDA ~US$6.3/t. FY27 bauxite target cut to 9-11 mn t; FY28 target of 15 mn t reaffirmed.
non_rep: Two operating Guinea ports and a beneficiation plant took years of capex (fixed assets ₹577 Cr at Mar-24 to ₹1,499 Cr at Mar-26) and government relationships to build; a proposed Guinean bauxite export-quota system (expected before end-2026) could favour incumbents with infrastructure. In India, four decades of mineral processing since 1982 and a promoter family that has raised its stake from 39.78% (Mar-20) to 48.04% (Jun-26).
tailwinds: Structural bauxite demand from new alumina refineries (four in China, +20-30 mn t demand estimated by management)
Guinea export-quota system expected before end-2026 could tighten supply and lift ex-works realisations
Port capacity build-out (Boffa 8 mtpa now, GSM 10 mtpa by Q4 FY27) supports the 15 mn t FY28 target
Freight normalisation would restore EBITDA/t toward the ~US$10 historical run-rate from US$6.3
Value-added bentonite (cat litter, foundry), kaolin for paper/paint and iron-ore commercialisation as new legs
risks: Single-commodity, single-country concentration: Guinea bauxite ~84% of turnover with margins hostage to ocean freight and Chinese alumina demand
Guinea political/regulatory risk (export quotas, fiscal terms) and low effective tax rate (5-6%) that may not persist
Rising leverage: borrowings ₹1,444 Cr at Mar-26 (₹758 Cr Mar-23) after four years of negative FCF (FY22-FY25); parent unrated

FY27 volume guidance already cut to 9-11 mn t; Q1 FY27 margin fell to 11.7%; sulphuric-acid prices up ~5x hurt bleaching clay

Status of the ASQ Connect pledge over Ashapura International shares and promoter succession (Chetan Shah to Chief-Strategy & Planning from 1 Oct 2026)
